:::{#def-complex-number}
#### Complex number

A **complex number** is a number of the form

$$z = a + b\,i,$$

where $a$ and $b$ are real numbers and $i$ is the imaginary unit (@def-imaginary-unit).
The set of all complex numbers is $\bbC \eqdef \{a + b\,i : a, b \in \reals\}$.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#def-real-part}
#### Real part

The **real part** of a complex number $z = a + b\,i$ (@def-complex-number) is $\operatorname{Re} z \eqdef a$.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#def-imaginary-part}
#### Imaginary part

The **imaginary part** of a complex number $z = a + b\,i$ (@def-complex-number) is $\operatorname{Im} z \eqdef b$.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#def-complex-equality}
#### Equality of complex numbers

Two complex numbers (@def-complex-number) are equal exactly when their real parts (@def-real-part) are equal and their imaginary parts (@def-imaginary-part) are equal.

:::

::: notes
@axler2024linear [Definition 1.1, p. 2] defines $\bbC$ as the set of ordered pairs $(a, b)$ of real numbers, written $a + bi$,
and @axler2024linear [Definition 4.1, p. 120] defines the real and imaginary parts.
:::
